h1:
Buriram Khmer Temple Circuit
Phanom Rung–Mueang Tam–Khao Angkhan
intro: Buriram's best Khmer temples sit close together in the same southern corner around Chaloem Phra Kiat and Prakhon Chai, so you can string them into a single loop. This plan lays out a smooth Phanom Rung–Mueang Tam–Khao Angkhan route, in both a tight one-day version and a relaxed two-day version where you can walk without rushing. You get an hour-by-hour timeline, opening hours, the real admission prices, and food stops along the way that you don't have to gamble on.

blocks.html: If you're coming to Buriram to take the stone temples seriously, the three you shouldn't skip are Phanom Rung, Mueang Tam and Khao Angkhan. Lucky for you, they all sit in the same zone in the south of the province, only a few dozen kilometres apart, so it's easy to make them one route. Phanom Rung is the grand temple on top of an extinct volcano. Mueang Tam is a lowland temple ringed by reservoirs, a completely different look. Khao Angkhan is a colourful temple on the rim of another volcanic crater. Cover all three and you get the full picture of Khmer civilisation in Buriram.

This plan is written for two styles. If you only have one day, you can squeeze it all in as long as you leave early. But if you'd rather walk slowly and shoot photos at an easy pace, we suggest spreading it over two days with one overnight, so you catch both the morning and evening light on the temples.

blocks.text: Why it works as one loop

blocks.html: The heart of this plan is how surprisingly close everything is. Phanom Rung is in Chaloem Phra Kiat district. Mueang Tam sits at the foot of Phanom Rung hill on the Prakhon Chai side, only about 8 km from Phanom Rung. Khao Angkhan is in Charoen Suk subdistrict, around 20 km from Phanom Rung. The three points form a small triangle. From Buriram town centre it's about 60–65 km to this zone, a little over an hour's drive.

The honest advice: you really want your own car or a rental, because public transport to these three spots is awkward and the connections are hard. If you're not driving yourself, the easier option is to charter a car from town or join a day trip that already runs this route.

blocks.text: Combo ticket and opening hours, check before you plan

blocks.html: The thing that saves money and makes planning easier is the combo ticket. The Fine Arts Department sells a single ticket covering both Phanom Rung and Mueang Tam: 30 THB for Thais, 150 THB for foreigners, cheaper than buying each separately. Bought separately, Phanom Rung is 20 THB for Thais and 100 THB for foreigners, and Mueang Tam is priced similarly. So if you're going to both anyway, the combo ticket is the better deal. Khao Angkhan is a temple, with no admission fee, just a donation if you wish.

items: Phanom Rung — open daily 08:30–16:30 · Thais 20 THB, foreigners 100 THB
Mueang Tam — open daily, hours close to Phanom Rung's · similar price, combo ticket available with Phanom Rung
Phanom Rung + Mueang Tam combo ticket — Thais 30 THB, foreigners 150 THB, one ticket gets you into both
Wat Khao Phra Angkhan — open daily, roughly 08:00–17:00 · no admission fee

blocks.title: Before you set off
blocks.html: All three spots are out of town and food on the hills is scarce. Fill up the tank and eat a proper breakfast before leaving town. The temple grounds have no shade and you'll be walking in the sun, so pack a hat and water. Khao Angkhan is a temple, so covering your shoulders and knees will keep things comfortable.

blocks.text: Plan A — the two-day, one-night temple loop

blocks.html: This is the version we like best, because you catch the morning and evening light on the temples without rushing. Day one is all about Phanom Rung and Mueang Tam at a full, unhurried pace. Stay the night around Nang Rong or head back into town, whichever you prefer. Day two you take in Khao Angkhan plus an extra stop or two. Great for anyone who likes photography and hates being rushed.

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Phanom Rung mid-morning, Mueang Tam in the afternoon

items.activity: Leave your accommodation in Buriram town, take Highway 218 then 24 toward the Chaloem Phra Kiat zone
items.note: It's about 60–65 km to Phanom Rung. Grab breakfast in town before you go.

items.activity: Arrive at Phanom Rung Historical Park, buy the Phanom Rung + Mueang Tam combo ticket, then walk up to the temple
items.note: Combo ticket is 30 THB for Thais, 150 THB for foreigners, and it also gets you into Mueang Tam.

items.activity: Follow the main axis along the naga bridge, the row of pillars and the stairway up to the central sanctuary, and see the Reclining Vishnu lintel
items.note: It's not too hot yet in the morning, so the climb is easy and the light is good.

items.activity: Come down from Phanom Rung and drive on to Mueang Tam at the foot of the hill on the Prakhon Chai side, about 8 km away
items.note: Use the same combo ticket to get in, no need to buy again.

items.activity: Break for lunch at a restaurant around Prakhon Chai or Nang Rong on the way back
items.note: Fill up properly so the afternoon walk is comfortable.

items.activity: Return to Mueang Tam for a closer look, walking around the L-shaped reservoirs and the gallery
items.note: Mueang Tam is a lowland temple, easier to walk than Phanom Rung and good for the afternoon.

items.activity: Check in to your accommodation, either around Nang Rong or back in Buriram town
items.note: Heading back into town gives you more dinner options.

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Khao Angkhan in the morning, an easy finish

items.activity: Leave your accommodation and head to Wat Khao Phra Angkhan in Charoen Suk subdistrict
items.note: If you stayed in Nang Rong it's not far. If you went back to town, allow a bit more driving time.

items.activity: Head up Khao Phra Angkhan to see the multi-coloured Buddha hall and the Dvaravati-era sandstone boundary stones
items.note: The morning sun is still gentle, easy for photos and paying respects.

items.activity: Take in the view over the surrounding fields from the high point, and rest with a drink before heading down
items.note: Khao Angkhan is another long-extinct volcano, with farms and fields all around.

items.activity: Come down the hill and find lunch on the way back into Buriram town
items.note: An easy way to close out the temple loop, with energy left to explore the town.

blocks.text: Plan B — squeezing the temple loop into one day

blocks.html: If you only have one day, it's doable, but you have to leave early and not dawdle. Line the route up so it flows one way: start at Phanom Rung mid-morning while the light is still good, stop at Mueang Tam right next door, have lunch around Prakhon Chai or Nang Rong, then head up Khao Angkhan in the afternoon. Cover all three before driving back into town in the evening.

blocks.label: One-day version
blocks.title: Phanom Rung–Mueang Tam–Khao Angkhan in one loop

items.activity: Leave Buriram town, take Highway 218 then 24 toward Phanom Rung
items.note: Fill the tank and eat breakfast before you go; food is scarce on the hills.

items.activity: Arrive at Phanom Rung, buy the combo ticket, walk up to the temple on top of the volcano
items.note: Allow about 1.5–2 hours including the climb.

items.activity: Drive on to Mueang Tam, about 8 km away, and walk around the reservoirs and gallery
items.note: Use the same combo ticket. Mueang Tam is easy to walk and takes about 45 min–1 hour.

items.activity: Break for lunch around Prakhon Chai or out toward Nang Rong
items.note: Fill up before heading up Khao Angkhan in the afternoon.

items.activity: Head up Wat Khao Phra Angkhan to see the multi-coloured hall and the viewpoint
items.note: The afternoon sun is strong, so pack a hat and water. Allow about 1 hour.

items.activity: Come down from Khao Angkhan and drive back into Buriram town
items.note: You'll reach town around 16:00–16:30, time to rest before finding dinner.

blocks.text: Food stops along the way, so you don't go hungry

blocks.html: The temple zone is out of town and food on the hills is limited. The sensible refuelling points are around Nang Rong and Prakhon Chai, both on the way through, with plenty of choices. To be blunt: don't wait until you're starving on the hill, because finding food up there is harder than you'd expect.

items.name: Kha Mu Nang Rong
items.blurb: A long-running stewed pork leg shop in Nang Rong on Chok Chai–Det Udom road, right on the route between town and Phanom Rung. Handy to fill up before or after the temples.

items.name: Lang Wang, Prakhon Chai
items.blurb: A half-cafe, half-restaurant in Prakhon Chai with Thai food and noodles, open late. A good stop after Mueang Tam.

items.name: Roadside spots on Highway 24
items.blurb: Around Nang Rong there are plenty of stir-fry and rice spots along the highway, easy to find as you drive in and out of the temple zone.

blocks.text: Want special light? Aim for the sun-through-the-doorways event

blocks.html: Phanom Rung is famous for the moment when the sun shines straight through all 15 doorways in a perfect line. It only happens a few times a year. The sunrise alignment falls on 2–4 April and 8–10 September, and the sunset alignment on 5–7 March and 5–7 October. Those days draw huge crowds, so you have to claim a spot well before dawn or before sunset. If you can plan your trip to land on those dates, you get a shot that's genuinely hard to come by. But on any ordinary day you can still enjoy the temple just as fully, you just won't catch the light through the doorways.

blocks.title: If you come during the doorway alignment
blocks.html: Rework the plan so Phanom Rung is your first stop before dawn or your last stop in the evening, depending on the light window, and fit Mueang Tam and Khao Angkhan into the rest of the day. The special light window only happens once, and if you miss it you wait a year.

blocks.text: Get the full range, how each temple differs

blocks.html: These three have different moods, they're not repeats of each other. Phanom Rung is the hilltop temple, with a long axis to walk up, grand in scale and rich with carved lintels. Mueang Tam is the lowland temple, its highlight being the four L-shaped reservoirs that surround it and the five-headed nagas at the water's edge, with lovely reflections and easier walking than Phanom Rung. Khao Angkhan is a later-era temple built on an old sacred site, remembered for its boldly coloured hall and the Buddha images lined up around it, plus the Dvaravati-era sandstone boundary stones that show this place was sacred even before the Khmer period.

Honestly, if you're expecting thousand-year-old stone temples at all three, Khao Angkhan is a different thing, because the architecture you actually see is later work, not an ancient Khmer monument like Phanom Rung and Mueang Tam. But seen as a temple with a good view on a volcano, where you can pay respects and take photos, it's worth the stop, and it sits right on the same route.

blocks.text: Want to add a little more? Extra stops on the same route

items: Khao Kradong — an extinct volcano near town, with a suspension bridge over the crater and the Phra Suphatbophit Buddha on top. A good stop on the way out or the way back into town.
Prasat Plai Bat — a group of Khmer temples in the same area, for temple enthusiasts who want to dig deeper.
Ban Khok Muang community — the community around Mueang Tam, with woven textiles and local life to drop in on if you have time to spare.

items.name: Tickets
items.blurb: Get the Phanom Rung + Mueang Tam combo ticket, 30 THB for Thais and 150 THB for foreigners, better value than buying separately. Khao Angkhan is free.

items.name: Departure time
items.blurb: Leaving before 8am lets you cover everything without rushing. With two days it's even more relaxed, with both morning and evening light for photos.

items.blurb: Hat, water, comfortable walking shoes, and a wrap for your shoulders at Khao Angkhan temple. There's no shade at all on the temple grounds.

faq.q: Can you do Phanom Rung, Mueang Tam and Khao Angkhan all in one day?
faq.a: Yes, if you have your own car and leave town before 8am. The three spots are in the same zone: Phanom Rung and Mueang Tam are about 8 km apart, and Khao Angkhan is around 20 km from Phanom Rung. Do Phanom Rung–Mueang Tam from morning to midday, then head up Khao Angkhan in the afternoon, and you'll cover everything before driving back into town in the evening. But if you'd rather walk at an easy pace, spreading it over two days is better.

faq.q: How much is admission to the Buriram temples, and is there a combo ticket?
faq.a: There's a single combo ticket for both Phanom Rung and Mueang Tam: 30 THB for Thais, 150 THB for foreigners, cheaper than buying each separately. Bought on its own, Phanom Rung is 20 THB for Thais and 100 THB for foreigners. Wat Khao Phra Angkhan is a temple with no admission fee, just a donation if you wish.

faq.q: Can you do the Buriram temple loop without your own car?
faq.a: It's possible but a hassle. Public transport to Phanom Rung, Mueang Tam and Khao Angkhan is limited and the connections are hard. The easier options are renting a car and driving yourself, chartering a car from Buriram town, or joining a day trip that already runs this route.

faq.q: Which one should you start with, Phanom Rung or Mueang Tam?
faq.a: We'd start at Phanom Rung in the morning while the sun is still gentle, because it has a long axis to walk up on top of the hill. Then come down to Mueang Tam, the lowland temple that's easier to walk, from late morning into the afternoon. Save Khao Angkhan for the afternoon or the next day. The exception is during the sun-through-the-doorways event, when you have to build the schedule around Phanom Rung's light window.

faq.q: How do Mueang Tam and Phanom Rung differ, and do you need to visit both?
faq.a: They're clearly different and you should visit both. Phanom Rung is the temple on top of a volcano, grand with its long axis and carved lintels. Mueang Tam is the lowland temple, with its standout L-shaped reservoirs and five-headed nagas, lovely water reflections and easier walking. They're only about 8 km apart and one combo ticket covers both, so there's no reason to skip either one.
